tests.title: NewRun exposes a 32-lowercase-hex session_id and keeps its signature
given: a clock and tool name for NewRun
tests.when: NewRun is called
then: Run exposes a session_id string matching ^[0-9a-f]{32}$
NewRun compiles with its existing signature and returns no error
the id is set before the sink, envelope or file-name functions are used
tests.pseudocode: r = NewRun(tool, args...); assert regex('^[0-9a-f]{32}$').match(r.SessionID()); assert len(r.SessionID()) == 32

tests.title: Session ids from distinct runs are well-formed and differ, with no pid/clock/host component
given: NewRun called with a frozen clock, and the same pid and host throughout
tests.when: for any N in 2..500 runs created by NewRun in the same process at the same instant
then: every session_id matches ^[0-9a-f]{32}$
all N session_ids are pairwise distinct
no id contains the hex of the pid or of the formatted started_at
tests.pseudocode: ids = [NewRun(...).SessionID() for _ in range(N)]; assert len(set(ids)) == N; for id in ids: assert re.match('^[0-9a-f]{32}$', id); assert hex(pid) not in id[:8]

tests.title: A flag-parse failure still emits an envelope with a session_id, on stdout and in the report
given: XDG_STATE_HOME is a temp dir
the App is real
tests.when: App.Main is run with an undefined flag --bogus
then: exit code is 2 and stage is usage
the stdout envelope has a session_id of 32 hex characters
the report file envelope has the same session_id
the report file name ends with that session_id and .json
tests.pseudocode: code = app.Main(['--bogus']); env = json(stdout); assert code == 2; assert re('^[0-9a-f]{32}$').match(env.session_id); assert json(read(report)).session_id == env.session_id

tests.title: The session id generator uses crypto/rand only and adds no module
given: go.mod and the source file that defines the generator
tests.when: the file's imports and go.mod's require block are inspected
then: the generator file imports crypto/rand and encoding/hex
it does not import math/rand or math/rand/v2
go.mod's require set is the same as the set recorded before this spec
tests.pseudocode: imports = parse_imports(file); assert 'crypto/rand' in imports; assert 'math/rand' not in imports; assert requires(go.mod) == EXPECTED

tests.title: Every event carries the header ts, tool, session_id, type in that key order
given: a sink built for a run with a known session_id and a buffer writer
tests.when: one event of each type is emitted through the sink
then: each line's first four keys are, in order, ts, tool, session_id, type
session_id equals the run's session id on every line
tests.pseudocode: for ev in ALL_EVENT_TYPES: sink.emit(ev); for line in lines: keys = ordered_keys(line); assert keys[:4] == ['ts','tool','session_id','type']; assert json(line).session_id == run.sid

tests.title: The envelope has a required session_id right after schema_version, identical on stdout and in the report, and described by --schema
given: XDG_STATE_HOME is a temp dir
tests.when: a tool is run with an invalid input (usage error), a successful run, and with --schema
then: session_id is the key immediately after schema_version in stdout and the report file
stdout and report session_id are equal for each run
the --schema document lists session_id as a string property and in required
tests.pseudocode: out = run(...); keys = ordered_keys(out.stdout); assert keys[keys.index('schema_version')+1] == 'session_id'; assert out.stdout.session_id == read(report).session_id; schema = run('--schema'); assert 'session_id' in schema.envelope.required

tests.title: run_end.report_file equals envelope.report_file, including the empty string when no report is written
given: XDG_STATE_HOME is a temp dir
one case where the report is written and one where --report-file points at an unwritable path
tests.when: each run completes and the last events line and the envelope are compared
then: run_end has a report_file key in both cases
it equals the envelope's report_file in both cases
it is the empty string when the report was not written
tests.pseudocode: for case in cases: env = stdout; last = json(lines(events)[-1]); assert last.type == 'run_end'; assert 'report_file' in last; assert last.report_file == env.report_file

tests.title: The events_file artifact follows report_file and appears only when the file was created, also under --dry-run
given: XDG_STATE_HOME is a temp dir for the normal and dry-run cases
an unwritable events parent for the no-file case
tests.when: a normal run, a --dry-run run and a run whose events file cannot be created finish
then: in the first two, artifacts ends with {kind: report_file} then {kind: events_file, path} in stdout and in the report file, and path names an existing file
in the third, artifacts has no events_file entry
the --schema artifact-kind enum contains events_file
tests.pseudocode: kinds = [a.kind for a in env.artifacts]; assert kinds.index('events_file') == kinds.index('report_file')+1; assert exists(artifact('events_file').path)

tests.title: DefaultReportPath and DefaultEventsPath share stem, timestamp format and state base
given: XDG_STATE_HOME=/s, started_at 2025-01-02T03:04:05Z, session id S
tests.when: both functions are called
then: report path is /s/agent-fox/runs/<tool>-<started_at>-S.json
events path is /s/agent-fox/events/<tool>-<started_at>-S.jsonl
the timestamp contains no colon
both stems are identical and both bases derive from the same stateHome()
tests.pseudocode: r = DefaultReportPath(tool, t, S); e = DefaultEventsPath(tool, t, S); assert stem(r) == stem(e); assert dir(dir(r)) == dir(dir(e)); assert ':' not in base(r)

tests.title: When stateHome() fails the run records both not-written warnings and keeps its exit code
given: XDG_STATE_HOME is unset and HOME is unset so os.UserHomeDir fails
tests.when: App.Main runs a valid dry-run invocation, and the same invocation runs with a good state dir
then: the exit codes of both runs are equal
the failing run's envelope warnings contain report_file_not_written and events_file_not_written, both stage report
no file is created
tests.pseudocode: bad = run(env={}); good = run(env={XDG_STATE_HOME: tmp}); assert bad.code == good.code; codes = {w.code:w.stage for w in bad.env.warnings}; assert codes['report_file_not_written']=='report' and codes['events_file_not_written']=='report'

tests.title: Report name, events name and envelope session_id always share the session id, and each file names the other
given: XDG_STATE_HOME is a temp dir per case
tests.when: for any tool in {spec, issue, fix, impl} and any valid invocation (normal, --dry-run, --preflight, --emit-events, --quiet)
then: the report file name, events file name and envelope session_id carry the same session id
envelope artifacts events_file.path is the events file on disk
run_end.report_file is the report on disk
tests.pseudocode: sid = env.session_id; assert base(report).endswith(sid+'.json'); assert base(events).endswith(sid+'.jsonl'); assert artifact('events_file').path == events; assert last_event.report_file == report

tests.title: The state directory resolves from XDG_STATE_HOME, else from the home directory, with runs/ and events/ beneath
given: case A: XDG_STATE_HOME=/x; case B: XDG_STATE_HOME unset and HOME=/h
tests.when: stateHome(), DefaultReportPath and DefaultEventsPath are called, and a run creates both
then: case A base is /x/agent-fox
case B base is /h/.local/state/agent-fox
reports live under runs/, events under events/, both created on demand
no environment variable other than XDG_STATE_HOME and HOME is read for this
tests.pseudocode: setenv(XDG_STATE_HOME,'/x'); assert stateHome() == '/x/agent-fox'; unsetenv; setenv(HOME,'/h'); assert stateHome() == '/h/.local/state/agent-fox'

tests.title: An empty XDG_STATE_HOME is treated as unset
given: XDG_STATE_HOME is the empty string and HOME is a temp dir
tests.when: stateHome() is called and a run writes its files
then: the base is $HOME/.local/state/agent-fox
files appear under that directory
tests.pseudocode: t.Setenv('XDG_STATE_HOME',''); t.Setenv('HOME',tmp); assert stateHome() == tmp+'/.local/state/agent-fox'

tests.title: --report-file moves only the report; the events file keeps its default path
given: XDG_STATE_HOME is a temp dir
--report-file points at another temp dir file
tests.when: App.Main runs with --report-file
then: the report is written at the given path
the events file exists at <state>/events/<tool>-<started_at>-<session_id>.jsonl
a glob events/*-<session_id>.jsonl finds exactly one file
tests.pseudocode: run(['--report-file', p, ...]); assert exists(p); assert len(glob(state+'/events/*-'+sid+'.jsonl')) == 1

tests.title: The events file is created exclusively with mode 0600 and a pre-existing file is never truncated
given: a run whose session id is fixed
a pre-existing file at the computed events path holding known bytes
tests.when: openEvents runs for a fresh path and then for the occupied path
then: the fresh file has mode 0600 and was opened with O_CREATE|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY|O_APPEND semantics
the occupied file is byte-for-byte unchanged
a events_file_not_written warning is recorded for the collision
tests.pseudocode: os.WriteFile(path, B, 0644); sink, warn = openEvents(run); assert read(path) == B; assert warn.code == 'events_file_not_written'; assert mode(freshPath) == 0600

tests.title: Directory and file modes: events/ 0700, parents 0755, existing events/ untouched, report modes unchanged
given: an empty state home in a temp dir; a second case with events/ pre-created with mode 0755
tests.when: a run completes in each case
then: events/ is 0700 and agent-fox/ and the state home created by the run are 0755
runs/ is 0755 and the report file 0644
the pre-existing events/ keeps 0755
tests.pseudocode: run(); assert mode(state+'/events') == 0700; assert mode(state) == 0755; assert mode(state+'/runs') == 0755; assert mode(report) == 0644

tests.title: Each event is exactly one Write call ending with a newline
given: a sink writing to a recording io.Writer that logs each Write call
tests.when: several events, including one with a very large field, are emitted
then: each recorded Write holds exactly one complete JSON line ending in \n with no embedded raw newline
the number of Writes equals the number of events
truncating the stream at any Write boundary leaves only complete lines
tests.pseudocode: for ev in events: sink.emit(ev); assert len(w.calls) == len(events); for c in w.calls: assert c.endswith('\n') and c.count('\n') == 1

tests.title: Runs that pass the sink build and end early leave an events file whose last line is run_end
given: XDG_STATE_HOME is a temp dir
tests.when: App.Main runs for: a later usage error, a failing input, a refused preflight, --preflight, and --dry-run
then: each run has one events file
the final line of each parses as JSON with type run_end
every line of the file is complete JSON
tests.pseudocode: for case in cases: run(case); lines = readlines(only_file(events)); assert json(lines[-1]).type == 'run_end'

tests.title: Invocations refused before the sink is built create no events file but still report
given: XDG_STATE_HOME is a temp dir
tests.when: App.Main runs with -h, --version, --schema, a bare invocation on a terminal, an undefined flag, --events-file x, --events jsonl, an invalid --detail, --total-budget, --input-kind, a bare invocation off-terminal, and an invalid --output
then: the events/ directory has no file after each run, and no empty file
for the usage-error cases a report is written and its artifacts have no events_file entry
exit codes are as before this change
tests.pseudocode: for case in cases: run(case); assert glob(state+'/events/*') == []; if case.is_usage_error: assert 'events_file' not in kinds(env.artifacts) and exists(report)

tests.title: An uncreatable events file yields a low events_file_not_written warning and an unchanged exit code
given: XDG_STATE_HOME/agent-fox/events is a regular file so the directory cannot be made
a reference run with a writable state directory
tests.when: App.Main runs with --emit-events
then: the envelope warnings hold events_file_not_written with severity low and stage report
stderr carries a warning event for it
the exit code equals the reference run's exit code
warncode.go lists the code and maps it to stage report
tests.pseudocode: writeFile(state+'/agent-fox/events','x'); r = run(['--emit-events',...]); w = find(r.env.warnings,'events_file_not_written'); assert w.severity=='low' and w.stage=='report'; assert any(json(l).type=='warning' for l in r.stderr_lines); assert r.code == ref.code

tests.title: With no file and no --emit-events the sink is inactive and no heartbeat starts
given: the events path cannot be created
EmitEvents is false
tests.when: openEvents builds the sink and the run proceeds past the heartbeat start point
then: sink.Active() is false
no heartbeat ticker or goroutine is started
stderr and stdout are the same as for a run without a sink
tests.pseudocode: s = openEvents(run_with_bad_dir, emit=false); assert not s.Active(); assert heartbeatStarted == 0

tests.title: The heartbeat ticks every 15 seconds for the whole run when an events file exists
given: a sink with an events file and a fake clock and ticker
tests.when: the fake clock advances by 15s three times, then the run ends
then: three heartbeat events are written to the file
none is written after run_end
the interval used is 15 seconds even in a run with no --emit-events
tests.pseudocode: for i in 1..3: clock.advance(15s); assert count('heartbeat') == 3; run.end(); clock.advance(15s); assert count('heartbeat') == 3

tests.title: --emit-events parses as a shared boolean flag setting Common.EmitEvents
given: the shared flag registration used by all four tools
tests.when: flags are parsed with and without --emit-events
then: Common.EmitEvents is true exactly when the flag is given
the flag takes no value and a following positional argument is not consumed
--help output lists --emit-events
tests.pseudocode: c = parse(['--emit-events']); assert c.EmitEvents; assert not parse([]).EmitEvents

tests.title: --quiet silences stderr under both --emit-events settings and leaves the file complete
given: XDG_STATE_HOME is a temp dir
tests.when: App.Main runs with --quiet, and with --quiet --emit-events
then: stderr is empty in both runs
each events file holds the full stream ending with run_end
tests.pseudocode: for flags in [['--quiet'],['--quiet','--emit-events']]: r = run(flags); assert r.stderr == ''; assert json(last(lines(events))).type == 'run_end'

tests.title: The removed flags and symbols no longer exist and the fix flag table is updated
given: the toolio source, cmd/fix/main.go and the flag set of each tool
tests.when: the package is inspected with go/parser and the flag sets are queried
then: there is no --events or --events-file flag definition
Common has no Events or EventsFile field and no ValidEvents, EventsText, EventsJSONL or events enum exists
the value-taking-flag table in cmd/fix/main.go has neither events nor events-file and has no emit-events entry
tests.pseudocode: assert fs.Lookup('events') is nil and fs.Lookup('events-file') is nil; assert 'EventsFile' not in fields(Common); assert 'emit-events' not in fixValueFlags

tests.title: --events-file in both spellings yields the removal usage error and no events file
given: XDG_STATE_HOME is a temp dir
tests.when: each tool runs with `--events-file out.jsonl` and with `--events-file=out.jsonl`
then: exit code is 2 and stage is usage
the message is exactly `--events-file was removed; events are always written to <state>/events/` with the literal text <state>/events/
a report is written and no events file is created
tests.pseudocode: for tool in TOOLS: for args in [['--events-file','o'],['--events-file=o']]: r = run(tool,args); assert r.code == 2 and r.env.stage == 'usage'; assert r.env.message == MSG; assert glob(events) == []

tests.title: --events in both spellings yields the rename usage error and no events file
given: XDG_STATE_HOME is a temp dir
tests.when: each tool runs with `--events jsonl` and with `--events=jsonl`
then: exit code is 2 and stage is usage
the message is `--events was renamed --emit-events`
a report is written and no events file is created
tests.pseudocode: r = run(['--events','jsonl']); assert r.code == 2 and r.env.stage == 'usage'; assert r.env.message == '--events was renamed --emit-events'; assert glob(events) == []

tests.title: With both removed flags only the first encountered is named
given: unsupportedFlagMessage and the flag-parse failure path
tests.when: args are `--events-file f --events jsonl` and then `--events jsonl --events-file f`
then: the first case's message contains the --events-file text and not the --events rename text
the second case's message contains the rename text and not the removal text
exactly one of the two texts appears in each message
tests.pseudocode: m1 = msg(['--events-file','f','--events','jsonl']); assert 'was removed' in m1 and 'was renamed' not in m1; m2 = msg(['--events','jsonl','--events-file','f']); assert 'was renamed' in m2 and 'was removed' not in m2

tests.title: Under --emit-events the stderr bytes equal the events file bytes
given: XDG_STATE_HOME is a temp dir and a scripted fake model
tests.when: for any run with --emit-events and any combination of --verbose, --show-text and a generated sequence of turns, tool calls and prose
then: stderr bytes are byte-for-byte equal to the events file content
tests.pseudocode: for scenario in gen_scenarios(): r = run(['--emit-events'] + flags); assert r.stderr == read(events_file(r))

tests.title: tool_call and text events are emitted without --verbose or --show-text
given: a Runner with Config.ShowText false and an Observer whose Verbose() is false, scripted to make two tool calls and produce prose
tests.when: the phase runs
then: two tool_call events and one text event reach the observer
the ToolCall hook is invoked for each call regardless of Verbose()
tests.pseudocode: obs = RecordingObserver(verbose=False); runner.Run(script); assert len(obs.toolCalls) == 2; assert len(obs.texts) == 1

tests.title: The sink records fields in full, unsanitised and unabbreviated
given: a sink with a buffer writer
tests.when: a text event holding 1 MiB of prose with ANSI escapes, tabs, unicode and a label-like prefix, and a tool_call with a 100 KiB arguments object, are emitted
then: the decoded text equals the input exactly
the decoded arguments equal the input exactly
no ellipsis, truncation marker or removed field is present
tests.pseudocode: sink.emit(Text{Text: big}); assert json(line).text == big; assert len(json(line2).arguments_raw) == len(args)

tests.title: The events file does not depend on --verbose, --show-text or --quiet
given: a deterministic scripted run and a fake clock
tests.when: for any combination of --verbose, --show-text and --quiet (8 combinations)
then: the events file has the same sequence of event types and the same field values apart from ts and durations in all combinations
tests.pseudocode: base = normalise(events(run([]))); for combo in subsets(['--verbose','--show-text','--quiet']): assert normalise(events(run(combo))) == base

tests.title: Begin prints unless --emit-events or --quiet is set, regardless of the sink
given: a Progress with an active sink and a captured stderr
tests.when: Begin is called with {neither, --emit-events, --quiet, both}
then: with neither it prints the spinner and a (duration) line on end
with --emit-events or --quiet it prints nothing and returns a usable no-op
the result does not change when the sink is made inactive
tests.pseudocode: p = NewProgress(sink=active, emit=False, quiet=False); end = p.Begin('x'); end(); assert stderr != ''; p2 = NewProgress(sink=active, emit=True); p2.Begin('x')(); assert stderr2 == ''

tests.title: Raw streams prose live only with --show-text and without --emit-events/--quiet, and never emits an event
given: a Progress with an active recording sink and captured stderr
tests.when: Raw('hello') is called for each combination of --show-text, --emit-events and --quiet
then: stderr receives exactly 'hello' only when --show-text is set and neither --emit-events nor --quiet is
stderr is empty in every other combination
the sink receives zero events from Raw in all combinations
tests.pseudocode: for st,em,q in product([0,1],repeat=3): p.Raw('hello'); assert stderr == ('hello' if st and not em and not q else ''); assert sink.events == []

tests.title: Without --emit-events stderr bytes match the pre-change baseline
given: recorded baseline stderr outputs captured from the pre-change code for a scripted run, with a fake clock and non-terminal and terminal modes
tests.when: for any combination of --verbose, --show-text and --quiet without --emit-events
then: stderr bytes equal the baseline for that combination, even though the events file is now always active
tests.pseudocode: for combo in combos: assert run(combo).stderr == BASELINE[combo]

tests.title: The text event has keys phase, turn, text after the header and no delta
given: a sink with a buffer writer
tests.when: Progress's per-turn text method is called with phase p, turn 2, text 'hi'
then: the line's keys in order are ts, tool, session_id, type, phase, turn, text
type is text
there is no delta key
tests.pseudocode: line = emitText('p',2,'hi'); assert keys(line) == ['ts','tool','session_id','type','phase','turn','text']

tests.title: A turn's text blocks are accumulated and joined with a newline, with no trailing newline, regardless of ShowText
given: a Runner with ShowText false fed TextDeltaEvent 'a', 'b', TextEndEvent, TextDeltaEvent 'c', TextEndEvent, then TurnEndEvent
tests.when: the events are processed
then: the text event's text is 'ab\nc'
it has no trailing newline
the result is identical with ShowText true
tests.pseudocode: feed(delta('a'),delta('b'),end,delta('c'),end,turnEnd); assert obs.texts[0].text == 'ab\nc'

tests.title: The text event is emitted directly before its turn event with the same turn number
given: a recording observer and a two-turn scripted stream, each turn with prose
tests.when: the phase runs to completion
then: in the sequence of observer calls each text call is immediately followed by the turn call
both carry the same turn number (1 then 2)
tests.pseudocode: seq = obs.calls; for i,c in enumerate(seq): if c.kind=='text': assert seq[i+1].kind=='turn' and seq[i+1].n == c.turn

tests.title: A turn with no prose emits no text event
given: a scripted stream with a turn containing only a tool call
tests.when: the turn ends
then: no text event is emitted for that turn
the turn event is still emitted
tests.pseudocode: feed(toolCallEnd, toolResult, turnEnd); assert obs.texts == []; assert len(obs.turns) == 1

tests.title: Prose buffered when a phase ends without a turn end is flushed once before phase_end with turn = completed+1
given: a stream with one completed turn, then prose in a second turn and then cancellation (and a variant with a stream error)
tests.when: the phase ends
then: a text event with turn 2 and the buffered prose precedes phase_end
exactly one such text event is emitted, never twice
the buffer is empty afterwards
tests.pseudocode: feed(turn1, delta('x')); cancel(); assert obs.calls[-2] == Text(turn=2,text='x'); assert obs.calls[-1].kind=='phase_end'; assert count(texts, 'x') == 1

tests.title: Observer has a per-turn text method that Progress implements by emitting a text event
given: the Observer interface, toolio.Progress and the hooks_test fake
tests.when: the new method is called on Progress with an active sink
then: toolio.Progress satisfies Observer at compile time
one text event reaches the sink
the fake in hooks_test records the call
tests.pseudocode: var _ agentrun.Observer = (*toolio.Progress)(nil); p.Text('ph', 3, 'body'); assert sink.last.type == 'text'

tests.title: tool_call carries phase, name, blocked, arguments, ok always, and exit_code/error only when set
given: a sink with a buffer writer
tests.when: tool_call events are marshalled for (a) an ok non-shell call, (b) an ok shell call with exit 0, (c) an error shell call with exit 1
then: arguments and ok are always present
exit_code is absent in (a) and present with value 0 in (b)
error is absent in (a)/(b) and present in (c)
omitempty is on exit_code and error only
tests.pseudocode: assert 'arguments' in a and 'ok' in a and 'exit_code' not in a and 'error' not in a; assert b.exit_code == 0 and 'error' not in b

tests.title: Arguments are recorded verbatim apart from whitespace and {} when empty
given: a Runner and a recording observer
tests.when: a ToolCallEndEvent arrives with input '{ "path": "a b",  "n": 1 }', then another with empty input
then: the first arguments is valid JSON equal to the compacted input
the second arguments is {}
tests.pseudocode: assert compact(in) == obs.calls[0].arguments; assert obs.calls[1].arguments == '{}'

tests.title: Invalid JSON tool input is recorded as a JSON string and the line is kept
given: a Runner, a recording observer and a real sink
tests.when: a tool call has input `{"a": ` (truncated)
then: the written line parses as JSON
arguments is a string equal to the raw input
the line is not dropped
tests.pseudocode: line = lastLine(); v = json(line); assert isinstance(v.arguments, str) and v.arguments == raw

tests.title: ok follows the result's error flag, not the exit status, and is false for a guard-refused call
given: results for: a non-error read, an error result, a shell result with IsError false and exit 1, a call refused by the shell guard
tests.when: each ToolResultEvent is processed
then: ok is true for the non-error read and the shell exit 1 with IsError false
ok is false for the error result and for the guard-refused call
blocked is true for the refused call
tests.pseudocode: assert [c.ok for c in calls] == [True, False, True, False]

tests.title: exit_code is recorded only for a shell call with a readable status, never guessed
given: shell results with a readable status 3, a shell result with no readable status, a refused shell call, and a non-shell tool result
tests.when: each is processed by the Runner
then: exit_code is 3 in the first case

tests.title: error is present exactly when ok is false and holds the result text or guard message
given: an error result with text 'boom', a refused call with guard message G, and a successful call
tests.when: each is processed

tests.title: Parallel calls to the same tool each carry their own arguments, matched by tool-call id, one event per call, without Verbose()
given: a Runner and an observer with Verbose() false
two ToolCallEndEvents for the tool 'read' with ids c1, c2 and different inputs, with results arriving in the order c2, c1
tests.when: the results arrive
then: exactly two ToolCall invocations, each taking a single struct argument

no result content appears in either

tests.title: Observer.ToolCall takes one struct with phase, name, blocked, arguments, ok, exit code and error
given: the Observer interface, the hooks_test fake and Progress
tests.when: the struct-based ToolCall is invoked with every field set
then: the code compiles with a single struct parameter
Progress writes a tool_call event with all supplied fields
the fake records the whole struct
